A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ATGC-Gen research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original promoter, enhancer, and ChIP-Seq generation experiments in Tables 2–4, plus conditioning, model-variant, and unmasking-rate analyses in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds analysis of motif occurrences and positions in generated promoter sequences in Appendix C.4.

M1.justification: Both versions retain sequence-level and feature-level conditioning, GPT and BERT variants, the same training objectives, and autoregressive or masked-recovery generation. v2 clarifies embeddings and unifies training-input notation without documenting an altered procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same human promoters, fly-brain and melanoma enhancers, and filtered GM12878 ChIP-Seq sequences. JASPAR supplies reference motifs for analyzing existing promoter outputs; it does not introduce a new generation task, sequence population, or test scenario.

E2.justification: The promoter baselines remain BIT Diffusion, D3PM-UNIFORM, DDSM, Dirichlet FM, and D3. Enhancer comparisons retain Dirichlet FM, and ChIP-Seq retains the same controls. Newly cited methods are not added to reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Appendix C.4 adds a motif-scanning protocol using ten JASPAR position frequency matrices, measuring sequences with at least one motif hit among 7,497 outputs and displaying five randomly selected positional examples. Existing benchmark settings, splits, and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused biological-plausibility analysis of motif occurrence and positional organization in generated promoters, presented in Appendix C.4 and Figures 4–5. The conditioning ablations, GPT/BERT comparison, and unmasking-rate analysis already present in v1 are retained.

E5.justification: Reporting remains based on point estimates, including the retained KS statistics. Neither version reports repeated-run variability, seed counts, or confidence intervals. The new motif frequencies and randomly selected examples do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 2–7 and Figure 3 remain unchanged. New Figure 4 reports motif hits in generated promoters, including GABPA in 7,285/7,497 sequences, KLF4 in 7,058/7,497, and YY1 in 6,242/7,497. Figure 5 adds positional observations from five sequences.

T1.justification: The projections, losses, and evaluation formulas retain their mathematical substance. v2's unified input notation, explicit column-vector shape, and equation renumbering clarify existing definitions. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction's three contributions retain the same claims: multimodal controllable DNA generation, a ChIP-Seq benchmark, and favorable experimental performance. The central conclusion remains unchanged; the motif analysis supplies additional support rather than redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 newly frames ATGC-Gen as generating candidates for experimental screening and explicitly acknowledges absent wet-lab validation. It also proposes experimental feedback and active learning. Appendix C.4 newly interprets motif frequencies and clustering as evidence of cis-regulatory elements and realistic regulatory grammar.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly describes the learnable DNA embedding layer and documents the new analysis's JASPAR motif accession identifiers and use of position frequency matrices. Appendices A–B retain the preprocessing, architectures, optimizer settings, hardware, and data-access information; the code link is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning through Bio-xLSTM, additional biomolecular language models, and a new cross-modality representation-learning discussion. It replaces v1's blanket assertion that existing studies do not involve generation with a narrower distinction concerning explicit heterogeneous-property conditioning. The Hyena hierarchy citation is removed, and JASPAR is newly cited.

P1.justification: Edits concentrate on related work, representation and training explanations, the motivation for variable-length ChIP-Seq data, and the discussion. Section 6 is renamed from Summary and Discussion to Conclusion and Discussion, and Appendix C.4 is added. Most prose and the overall section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a document-wide journal layout with a redesigned author block, publication headers, changed typography and margins, and resized or repositioned displays. It also adds the motif-frequency chart and positional map as Figures 4–5. Existing tables and Figures 1–3 preserve their substantive contents.

improvement.justification: v2 improves research positioning, explains existing method details more clearly, explicitly acknowledges absent wet-lab validation, and adds inspectable motif evidence. These are useful but limited gains: benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new motif analysis lacks a reported background comparison or scanning threshold, so its stronger enrichment and regulatory-grammar interpretations are not established by the plots alone.
